rationale: This is primarily a user-generated-content platform agreement rather than a digital storefront, and it is unusually clear that users retain ownership of their own content while gaining no ownership of the Service itself; 'Purchases and Memberships' are referenced only in passing without any deceptive 'buy' framing to analyze. However, it carries real consumer risk elsewhere: YouTube can terminate access at its 'sole discretion' for commercial-viability reasons, caps its total liability at $500, and shortens the time to sue to one year, all wrapped in dense legalese and capitalized boilerplate.
